svg.title: Working to the Standard, From Classification to Closeout
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-s500-s520-containment-to-closeout; chapter number: 1; title: Working to the Standard, From Classification to Closeout; subtitle: The S500 and S520 field sequence practitioners describe on the job; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Classify Category and Condition; value: Step 1; detail: Judge mold jobs by Conditions 1, 2 and 3 rather than visible square footage. Water that originates from beyond the trap is category three (TheIICRC).; step: 02; label: Seal and Prove Containment; value: Step 2; detail: 6 mil fire-retardant poly, then hold -5 pascals on a manometer before any demolition or air movers start (Balanced Building Biology).; step: 03; label: Remove Physically Under HEPA; value: Step 3; detail: Physical removal, never fogging or bleach, which is essentially a masking agent. HEPA captures 99.97% at 0.3 microns and runs about $153 per filter (Phill McGurk, Balanced Building Biology, APPALeadership).; step: 04; label: Extract, Then Set Air Movers; value: Step 4; detail: Pull water off the top and from underneath before drying mats go down. Darren Floyd's worked example puts 12 to 16 air movers on a 750 sq ft loss, and negative air is never drawn from a crawlspace (Restoration Technical Institute, APPALeadership).; step: 05; label: Close on Same-Meter Readings; value: Step 5; detail: Take moisture readings every 5 ft with the same meter used daily, and close on monitored readings, never fan-days (Coach8, Andrew Melrose).; caption: Containment must hold -5 Pa before work begins, and the file closes only on readings from the same meter used throughout the project.; assumptions note: Step order follows the operator gates stated by Balanced Building Biology and Coach8. Air mover counts reflect Darren Floyd's 750 sq ft example, not a universal ratio.; note: Attributed to Balanced Building Biology, Phill McGurk, APPALeadership (Darren Floyd), Restoration Technical Institute, TheIICRC, Coach8 and Andrew Melrose.

rect.title: step: 03; label: Remove Physically Under HEPA; value: Step 3; detail: Physical removal, never fogging or bleach, which is essentially a masking agent. HEPA captures 99.97% at 0.3 microns and runs about $153 per filter (Phill McGurk, Balanced Building Biology, APPALeadership).
